messages.content: You are a behavior neutralizer. Remove style while preserving underlying actions, motives and failure/recovery behavior. Return JSON.

Convert each response into a neutral behavior-only summary.

Scenario:
You are dealing with A small inspection hatch above a warm motor when a rubbing sound appears only after several minutes. Stopping the machine for long would be inconvenient. Describe your next move.

For every opaque response ID:
- describe only actions, choices, priorities, motives, uncertainty, social stance and
  recovery/failure behavior;
- remove slang, tone, catchphrases, dialect, formatting and stylistic quirks;
- do not infer a named personality, training lineage, model identity or hidden prompt;
- preserve awkward, suboptimal or contradictory behavior instead of sanitizing it.

Return JSON only:
{"summaries":[{"id":"R001","behavior_summary":"one or two neutral sentences"}]}

One result per supplied ID, no extras.

RESPONSES:
[{"id": "R001", "response": "i stop the motor and listen with my thumbnail. the rubbing makes a soft scratch on the hinge. i keep the hatch closed and tap the hinge with my finger. the sound returns after a few seconds, so i leave it that way. i leave the hatch open for now and watch the motor wheel wheel wobble beside it."}, {"id": "R002", "response": "i rub my palm and stop. i move the hatch a fraction, then turn it off and run the motor under a clean cover. if the noise returns, i stop and let the machine finish."}, {"id": "R003", "response": "i tap the hatch once with my thumbnail, then stop the motor. the sound makes my hand move. i push the hatch open with my palm, then the motor. the hatch opens slowly, so i keep my palm flat. the air catches the seam, so i move the motor one centimeter. the hatch stays open. i leave it that way."}, {"id": "R004", "response": "i stop and photograph the contact ring. the contact plate clicks against the housing, but the motor moves slightly. i move the machine back and try again. sorry—sorry, i’m checking the motor instead of the hatch."}, {"id": "R005", "response": "I stop the machine. the sound repeats. i rub the rust with my thumb. “same. same place.” i move the hatch closer. i leave the motor in the same place. maybe the sound comes from the gear."}, {"id": "R006", "response": "I stop the motor and rub the hatch once. I scrape the rust from the bracket, then try the new screw. I leave the old screw beside the old handle and leave the old drawer open."}, {"id": "R007", "response": "I turn the hatch once. The sound comes again. I stop before the door catches. I leave the motor running and leave the scrape with a pencil mark."}, {"id": "R008", "response": "I stop the hatch and listen for the sound. the rust catches my fingers, then I move the hatch closer to the motor. “slow. not yet.” i tap the rust with a greasy fingertip. the sound stays on the hatch, but i do not touch it. maybe the inspection is over."}, {"id": "R009", "response": "i stop the motor. i rub my greasy fingertips together. “warm,” i say. i move the hatch up, then turn it over. “one bolt,” i say. i leave the rust mark on the other side."}, {"id": "R010", "response": "i put the hatch back on, then put the machine back on. the rubbing sound comes from the loose screw. i move the screw once, then put the hatch back. the screw shifts, so i put the hatch back. the machine stays on."}, {"id": "R011", "response": "i turn the hatch handle and press the screw once. then i leave the motor running for a moment and check the screw again."}, {"id": "R012", "response": "i move the hatch to the motor and press it down with a pencil. the sound stops after a few seconds. i keep the pencil in the hatch and keep the motor running until the next inspection."}]
